drills.prompt: この{部屋|へや}から、{夜|よる}は{星|ほし}がたくさん＿＿。
drills.en: From this room you can see lots of stars at night.

options.why: 星 has が: the stars are what's visible. 見える = come into view, no one doing anything.
見る needs a person looking at something with を. 星が見ます makes the stars the ones looking.
見せる = show someone. The stars aren't showing anything to anyone.

drills.scene: Hotel check-in. The clerk asks for your passport.
drills.prompt: パスポートを＿＿ください。

options.why: The clerk wants to end up looking at it, so you have to make them see it: 見せる, show.
パスポートを見てください = please look at the passport (yourself). Grammatical, but the clerk would be asking you to read your own passport.
見える takes が for the thing that's visible, and you can't ask something to be visible with ください.

drills.prompt: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は、よく{一人|ひとり}で＿＿。
drills.en: On my days off I often go out by myself.

options.why: Going out on an outing, with no particular place → 出かける.
出す needs something with を that you take out or send. There's no thing here, just you going out.
出る needs a place you leave (家を出る) or something coming out. On its own, 一人で出ます sounds unfinished: leaving what?

drills.prompt: {明日|あした}は{六時|ろくじ}に{家|いえ}を＿＿。
drills.en: Tomorrow I leave the house at six.

options.why: Leaving a place → 出る, and the place takes を as the path you leave from.
出かける is going out on an outing; it doesn't take the place you leave with を. Say 六時に出かけます without 家を.
家を出します would mean you take the house out, or send it somewhere.

drills.prompt: この{店|みせ}は、お{寿司|すし}が＿＿います。
drills.en: At this shop, the sushi goes round (on a belt).

options.why: お寿司 has が: the sushi goes round by itself → 回る, the "it happens" side. (That's why it's called 回転寿司.)
-su = doing it. 回す needs someone turning something with を. With が on the sushi it doesn't fit.
曲がる is bending or turning a corner, not going round and round.

drills.prompt: {毎朝|まいあさ}、{一人|ひとり}で{公園|こうえん}を{一回|いっかい}＿＿。
drills.en: Every morning I go once around the park by myself.

options.why: You're the one going round, and 公園を is the path, not an object. Moving verbs take を for the route and stay on the "it happens" side.
公園を回します would mean you spin the park. The を here isn't an object, it's a route.

drills.scene: A bike is coming down the narrow lane. Warn your friend.
drills.prompt: あ、{後|うし}ろに＿＿ください！

options.why: Your friend moves back: they are the thing moving, there's no を → 下がる (-aru, it happens).
下げる needs something you lower or move back with を (いすを下げて). Here nothing is being moved but the person.

drills.prompt: {空|そら}に{黒|くろ}い{雲|くも}が＿＿います。
drills.en: Black clouds are spreading across the sky.

options.why: 雲 has が: the clouds spread on their own → 広がる (-aru). With ている, it's happening now.
広げる is spreading something out yourself (地図を広げる). No one is spreading the clouds.

drills.scene: A friend hands you a print from your film camera.
drills.prompt: この{写真|しゃしん}、{私|わたし}も＿＿いますか。
drills.en: Am I in this photo too?

options.why: 写る = to show up in a photo, the "it happens" side. 私も写っていますか = am I in it too.
写す is copying or photographing something with を. 私も写していますか would ask whether you're also taking (copying) something.
私も見えていますか = can I be seen too? Close, but it's about being visible, not about being in the picture.

drills.scene: Field recording by the harbor. The recorder goes dead.
drills.prompt: あ、レコーダーの{電池|でんち}が＿＿。
drills.en: Oh no, the recorder's battery ran out.

options.why: 電池 has が and it ran out on its own → 切れる (be cut, run out), the "it happens" partner of 切る.
切る is cutting something with を. The battery didn't cut anything.
電池が出ました = the battery came out (of its slot). A different problem.

drills.scene: A friend asks about your photos. Say you'll show them.
drills.why: You make them see the photos → 見せる with を. が + 見えます would be "the photos are visible."

drills.scene: Planning a day trip with a friend. Ask what time you're heading out.
drills.en: What time do you go out?
drills.why: A time takes に; going out on an outing is 出かける, no を needed. 出しますか would ask what time they send something.
